board.name: Vermont Board of Medical Practice (Department of Health)

ce.categoryRules: 100 approved credit hours every two years, at least 50 Category 1; proof submitted with the renewal application (Board Rule 32.4.1, eff. 5/1/2024)
ce.nccpaNote: Rule 32.4.2: NCCPA certification or recertification during the two year period may be accepted in lieu of the 100 hours. The rule does not make current NCCPA certification a renewal condition. The Board's October 2021 PA renewal instructions asked for proof of current NCCPA certification; that document predates the 2024 rule.

topicMandates.topic: Controlled substances prescribing (abuse and diversion, safe use, storage and disposal, VPMS use, risk assessment, alternatives to opioids, tapering, State and federal law)
topicMandates.appliesTo: PAs who prescribe controlled substances; anyone holding a DEA number or with a pending DEA application is presumed to prescribe. Must be AMA PRA Category 1, AAPA Category 1, or Board designated.

ce.controlledSubstanceCe: 2 hours each renewal for PAs who prescribe controlled substances (Board Rule 32.4.3, eff. 5/1/2024).

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Written practice agreement with a participating physician, filed with the Board before practice (electronically allowed). Reviewed during the 90 days before submitting each renewal application; the review is documented in writing and signed by the PA and reviewing physician; a revised agreement is signed and submitted to the Board. A new agreement must reach the Board before practice with each new employer or practice setting beyond the agreement's limits.
practice.notes: No supervision ratio or co-signature; a physician must be reachable for consultation at all times. Practice agreement review date must be documented.

prescribing.ceForPrescribers: 2 hours controlled substance prescribing CME each renewal for PAs who hold or have applied for a DEA number (Rule 32.4.3). VPMS registration required for any Schedule II to IV prescriber.

facts.quote: Licenses shall be renewed every two years on payment of the required fee.

facts.value: January 31 of even-numbered years
facts.cite: Board of Medical Practice, Applications, Licensing & Fees page
facts.quote: PA renewals occur January 31st of even years.

facts.value: practice agreement
facts.quote: only if the physician assistant has entered into a written practice agreement as set forth in subsection (b) of this section.

facts.value: filed with the Board
facts.quote: The practice agreement shall be filed with the Board. The Board shall not request or require any modifications to the practice agreement.

facts.value: reviewed at least at each licence renewal
facts.quote: at a minimum, at the time of the physician assistant’s license renewal.

facts.value: within 90 days before renewal application
facts.quote: must be reviewed, and if necessary updated, during the 90 days preceding submission of the physician assistant’s renewal application.

facts.value: new agreement filed before practice with each new employer
facts.quote: A new practice agreement must be received by the Board before a physician assistant may practice after a change in employment.

facts.value: PA prescribing controlled substances must hold DEA registration
facts.quote: A physician assistant who prescribes controlled substances shall be registered with the federal Drug Enforcement Administration.

facts.value: VPMS registration required for Schedule II to IV prescribers
facts.quote: Each health care provider who prescribes any Schedule II, III, or IV controlled substances shall register with the VPMS

facts.value: Board renewal instructions dated Oct 31 2021 asked for proof of current NCCPA certification (superseded by Rule 32.4.2, eff. 5/1/2024)
facts.cite: Board of Medical Practice PA Renewal Instructions, Oct 31 2021
facts.quote: Proof of current NCCPA certification.
facts.reason: Document is from 2021; the current rule (32.4.2) makes NCCPA certification an alternative to the 100 hours, not a renewal condition.

facts.value: 2021 instructions: 2 hours for PAs with DEA (now confirmed by Rule 32.4.3)
facts.cite: Board of Medical Practice PA Renewal Instructions, Oct 31 2021
facts.quote: PAs who have a DEA must have 2 hours of qualifying CME on Controlled Substances Prescribing.

facts.value: Rule 24.1.6 covers physician licensees; PAs are covered separately by Rule 32.4.3
facts.quote: All physician licensees who are required to certify completion of CME and who prescribe controlled substances shall certify at the time of each renewal

facts.value: practised within last 3 years or Board update of knowledge and skills
facts.quote: shall have practiced as a physician assistant within the last three years or have complied with the requirements for updating knowledge and skills
all physician assistants shall complete a continuing medical education program of 100 approved credit hours every two years.

facts.value: minimum 50 Category 1
facts.quote: A minimum of 50 credit hours shall be from Category 1.
Certification or recertification by the NCCPA at any time during a 2 -year licensure period may be accepted in lieu of 100 hours

facts.value: 2 hours each renewal for PAs who prescribe controlled substances
facts.quote: All licensees who prescribe controlled substances shall certify at the time of each renewal that they have completed at least two hours of CME

facts.value: DEA holders and pending applicants presumed to prescribe
facts.quote: who holds a D.E.A. number to prescribe controlled substances, or who has submitted a pending application for one, is presumed to prescribe

facts.value: review documented in writing and signed; revised agreement submitted to Board
facts.quote: The review must be documented in writing at the time that it is completed and signed by the physician assistant and reviewing physician.

facts.value: PA licences expire January 31 of even years

board.name: Vermont State Board of Nursing (Office of Professional Regulation, Secretary of State)

rn.ceHoursPerCycle: 20 hours in two years is one of several alternatives: 400 practice hours in 2 years, OR 960 in 5 years, OR 20 CE hours in 2 years, OR current national certification

aprn.title: APRN (role and population focus, e.g. nurse practitioner)
aprn.separateLicenceOrCertificate: separate APRN licence (requires Vermont RN or multistate compact RN licence)
aprn.practiceHoursPerCycle: 400 hours APRN practice in 2 years or 960 hours in 5 years

topicMandates.topic: Controlled substances: abuse and diversion, safe use, storage and disposal, VPMS, risk assessment, alternatives to opioids, tapering, law
topicMandates.appliesTo: APRNs with a DEA registration, a pending DEA application, or who dispense controlled substances

prescribing.controlledSubstanceCe: 2 hours per licensing period for APRNs with DEA (2016 Act 173 Sec. 9, uncodified session law); not listed in the June 2026 APRN renewal instructions
prescribing.notes: VPMS registration required for Schedule II to IV prescribers (18 V.S.A. § 4289(b)(1)); DEA registration is per state.

practice.agreementType: collaborative provider agreement during transition to practice only
practice.transitionToPracticeHours: 24 months and 2,400 hours in the initial role and population focus; 12 months and 1,600 hours for each additional role and population focus
practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: APRN keeps signed and dated copies; a current agreement must be presented at renewal if still in transition; Board notified (attestation form) when transition is complete.

facts.cite: Vermont Board of Nursing Administrative Rules 4-3 (eff. May 11, 2023)
facts.quote: Licenses are valid for fixed, two-year periods.

facts.value: 400 hours in 2 years or 960 hours in 5 years
facts.quote: Have practiced for a minimum of 50 days (400 hours) in the two years preceding application or 120 days (960 hours)

facts.value: 20 hours CE in 2 years (alternative)
facts.quote: Have completed 20 hours of qualifying continuing education in the two years immediately preceding the application; or

facts.value: national certification (alternative)
facts.quote: Hold a current nationally recognized certification.
This subchapter is the Vermont adoption of the Nurse Licensure Compact as amended by the National Council of State Boards of Nursing.

facts.value: RN renewal + APRN practice hours + national certification + collaborative agreement if required
facts.quote: Have practiced in an APRN role for a minimum of 50 days (400 hours) in the two years preceding application
possession of a current certification by a national APRN specialty certifying organization

facts.value: no general CE hour requirement listed for APRN renewal
facts.quote: upload current certification by a national APRN certifying organization for each specialty area of practice

facts.value: 24 months and 2,400 hours
facts.quote: An APRN with fewer than 24 months and 2,400 hours of licensed active advanced nursing practice in an initial role and population focus

facts.value: APRN maintains signed and dated copies
facts.quote: An APRN shall have and maintain signed and dated copies of all required collaborative provider agreements.

facts.value: solo practice permitted after transition; Board notified
facts.quote: An APRN who satisfies the requirements to engage in solo practice pursuant to subsection (a) of this section shall notify the Board

facts.value: 2 hours per licensing period for APRNs with DEA
facts.quote: shall complete a total of at least two hours of continuing education for each licensing period beginning on or after July 1, 2016

facts.value: VPMS registration required
facts.quote: Each health care provider who prescribes any Schedule II, III, or IV controlled substances shall register with the VPMS

facts.value: separate DEA registration per state
facts.quote: The DEA requires that a practitioner obtain a separate DEA registration in each state.

facts.value: expiration date printed on licence; expires at midnight on that date
facts.quote: Expiration dates are printed on licenses. A license expires if not renewed by midnight on the date of expiry.

facts.value: Nurse Licensure Compact effective February 1, 2022
facts.quote: The Vermont Nurse Licensure Compact became effective February 1, 2022.

facts.value: renewal needs practice requirement, national certification, collaborative agreement if in transition
facts.quote: (3) a current collaborative provider agreement if required for transition to practice.

unverified: PA hospice, palliative care or pain management 1 hour: Rule 24.1.5 and 26 V.S.A. § 1400(b) apply it to physician licensees; Rule 32.4.2 says PAs must also meet 'any applicable' CME set by law or rule, but nothing loaded applies 24.1.5 to PAs. Treat as not a PA requirement until the Board confirms.

PA current NCCPA certification at renewal: requested in the Board's October 2021 renewal instructions only; the 2024 rule makes NCCPA an alternative to the 100 hours. Whether the current online renewal still asks for NCCPA proof is not confirmed.
RN/APRN calendar expiry date: rule 4-3 says the date is printed on the licence; no primary page loaded states the calendar date.

APRN controlled substance CE: Act 173 (2016) Sec. 9 is uncodified session law and is not restated in the 2023 nursing rules or the June 2026 APRN renewal instructions; how OPR collects the attestation is unconfirmed (the requirement itself is confirmed).
No separate Vermont state controlled substance registration for individual prescribers was found (only DEA plus VPMS registration); absence not confirmed by an explicit primary statement.
